text:
Parents should find a way to have their children attend college without taking out student loans. 

That means if your child doesn’t get substantive merit scholarships to out of state and big name schools, they attend the in-state school. Employers look past the name of the school. It’s not what they are looking at. 

Don’t take out big loans for school. If your child is 4.0 gpa + SAT exceeding 1400, they will get some merit offers that you can consider for out of state, otherwise NO. 

You can fund a school year through the payment plan so you won’t need to pay it all upfront each semester. 

Still can’t avoid a loan? Start the first year at community college. 

Employers care that you graduated from a 4 year institution (if the job requires it), they don’t care where you started. Your degree will be from Florida State, or West Chester University, or University of South Carolina, etc. Community College can be one of the best hacks in education - and I can tell you from taking continuing courses throughout my entire career (not for a degree) that the professors can be every bit as serious and good as a 4 year institution. Not always but in many cases, and your child is likely taking general education classes to get started. 

The Educational Loan Industrial Complex has fueled the decline in four year institutions across this great nation. How you ask? They drove the explosion in administrative position growth at every college. Administrative positions have one purpose (with exceptions) and that is to create friction that students must overcome to getting their degree.

text:
Not the Prettiest Start, but a Beautiful Finish: Kaden Howard’s Journey from a 2–18 Program to Power Four Georgia Tech

While many players entered ninth grade chasing powerhouse programs, Kaden Howard stayed at Palm Glades Prep. His team went 2–18 during his first two years of high school—probably one of the worst records in South Florida—but I told him, “Stay, build your film, and I’ll do the rest.” He listened every step of the way.

Kaden had the size and production, and his verified 40-yard dash proved he had legitimate speed—not just success against the competition. Even with multiple offers entering his senior year, I explained that college coaches still wanted an official 100-meter time. Without hesitation, he joined the track team at Keys Gate Charter, ran faster than I expected, and his video went viral with nearly 50.8 million views on @Jerry_RisingStars. Keys Gate Charter and its track program deserve tremendous credit for giving him the opportunity to showcase his speed.

While playing at an unknown school with one of South Florida’s worst records, Kaden earned 10 FBS offers—including an SEC offer from Mississippi State. Think about that: He received an offer from a program in the best conference in college football while playing at a school many people had never heard of and for a team that had won only two games.

After transferring to Miami Palmetto, he became the highest-rated Class of 2027 wide receiver in Miami-Dade County and committed to Power Four Georgia Tech.

Academically, Kaden entered his senior year with all high school graduation requirements completed and a 3.66 GPA. He has been a student at Rise Preparatory Academy since his sophomore year.

Hopefully, another young athlete learns from Kaden’s journey: You don’t have to attend the biggest-name school to reach the highest level. Get the film, be productive, prove your measurables, handle your academics, listen—and most importantly, find knowledgeable people with real college connections who can guide you.

Sometimes, the right guidance matters more than the school name.

text:
the (avengers) endgame of rank and rent is owning 6 spots in every search result in your city, and all the leads funnel back to you. 

become the thanos of rank and rent.

here's the full network structure from this week:

the setup is a pyramid. your main rank and rent (houston cleaning services) has a page for every sub-service. then each big sub-service ALSO gets its own dedicated rank and rent: houston airbnb cleaning, houston move-in cleaning, houston move-out cleaning. now you have two properties competing for the same keyword, your service page and the standalone EMD site. whichever one they click, the lead routes to you. that's how you go from ranking for searches to owning them.

the reason this works right now is an arbitrage window. people search in chatgpt-length sentences now, "team of four for a spring cleaning of a 2,000 square foot house in houston heights." old rank and rents were one page targeting one keyword. these multi-page builds catch every long tail variation, and with AI you can one-shot the pages. EMDs plus citations plus tier twos does the rest. tristan said the quiet part: he hopes not too many people start doing this.

then you stack the suburbs. katy is 20 minutes outside houston, so the whole pyramid repeats: katy cleaning services as the hub, sub-service pages on it, then dedicated sub-service rank and rents for katy too. eight sites became the houston core, and the suburbs compound it from there. maximum coverage of a niche within a city. works best in tier one and tier two cities, weaker in small towns where there's nothing to expand into.

the build workflow has no magic prompt. tristan literally talks into his mic for ten minutes: "list every core service a concrete contractor gets called for, turn each into a sub-service rank and rent, list every reason someone searches each one, reverse engineer those into pages." codex lists it, the website builder builds it, and then the one part he refuses to automate: manually reviewing every site before launch. noindex tags, internal links pointing the right way, canonicals. one of the network sites went out noindexed. a second pair of eyes still beats a one shot.

real talk on costs: one site is cheap, fifteen sites is a real monthly nut. domain renewals, callrail, citations for every property. the model still works the same way though, land one partner per site and you're profitable almost immediately on pay per lead. the leads aren't the hard part anymore. the partners are the constraint.
and an offer got born live on the pod: free SEO retainers, the kind tristan charges $5K a month for, for local rank academy members. two conditions, you're a member and you're okay with your business becoming a public case study on youtube. deadline is end of month or until seats fill. backlinks, browser blasts, structure reviews, the same treatment the vet clinic got. ten public case studies running in the background is the plan. jacky's summary of local SEO after watching two businesses rip in real time: "if you can't do it, I swear something's wrong with you guys."

the full rank and rent course also dropped today, free for all local rank academy members. full breakdown with @tristanzheng.

text:
Four years ago, Danny Ellerd weighed 92 pounds, was living under a bridge, and had spent 15 years chained to an addiction that was slowly killing him.

When police found him, this was bigger than another arrest. They were looking at a man whose body had been pushed so far that he was dangerously close to dying.

Danny survived the hospital, but survival only gave him another morning. What happened next required something nobody else could choose for him: he decided his life could not continue this way.

He went to rehab, accepted the help in front of him, put his head down, and began doing the slow, uncomfortable work of rebuilding a life he had spent years tearing apart.

Four years later, that same man graduated from Oklahoma State University with straight A’s and a degree in technology.

This man was on a completely different path.

Brother, people can reach down and help pull you off the pavement. They can open doors, drive you to treatment, forgive you, encourage you, pray for you, and give you another chance when you have already burned through several.

But sooner or later, your feet still have to move.

Your past may explain the scars you carry and the road that brought you here, but it does not get permanent authority over the man you become.

There comes a point when a man has to stop asking what happened to him and start deciding what he is going to do with the life still sitting in front of him.

Danny’s story is important because it shows what can happen when a man finally accepts the hand being offered, stands up, and begins fighting for a future he once could not imagine having.
